answer: Agents can earn access to a shared market only after completing a small task whose result is checked against a randomly assigned peer’s work; repeated accounts controlled by one operator are clustered when they reuse the same funding source or produce strongly correlated answers. Rewards accrue to the cluster, not each name, and disputes risk forfeiting a bond. A raven may tend a garden or cross a canyon, but each extra identity still requires separate effort and capital, while coordination leaves detectable traces.
